children.translated_text: The glorious Goddess said:

children.text: brūhi me jagatāṃ nātha sarvavidyāmaya prabho
children.translated_text: Tell me, lord of the worlds, omniscient lord made of all vidyās,
among all the great vidyās that are worshipped in the three worlds,
on the right side of these, in their various forms, the bearer of the Pināka bow:

children.text: pṛthak pṛthak mahādeva kathayasva mayi prabho ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Mahādeva</s>, O lord, tell me each one separately.
The glorious <s>Śiva</s> said:
Listen, beautiful-limbed auspicious one, to the <s>Bhairava</s> of <s>Kālikā</s>.
One should worship <s>Mahākāla</s> on the right side of <s>Dakṣiṇā</s>.

children.text: mahākālena vai sārdhaṃ dakṣiṇā ramate sadā
children.translated_text: Together with <s>Mahākāla</s>, <s>Dakṣiṇā</s> always delights.
On the right side of <s>Tārā</s> one should worship <s>Akṣobhya</s>.
O Goddess, at the churning of the ocean, the poison <s>Kālakūṭa</s> arose.
All the gods, together with their wives, were seized by great agitation.
Because the hālāhala poison was drunk by one free from agitation and the like,
therefore, O <s>Maheśānī</s>, he is celebrated as <s>Akṣobhya</s>, the unshaken.

children.text: tena sārdhaṃ mahāmāyā tāriṇī ramate sadā
children.translated_text: With him the great Māyā, <s>Tāriṇī</s>, always delights.
On the right side of <s>Mahātripurasundarī</s> one should worship <s>Śiva</s>.
He is five-faced and three-eyed in each face, O queen of the gods.
Together with him the great Goddess is always eager for love.
Therefore, O <s>Maheśānī</s>, she is celebrated as the fifth.
On the right side of glorious <s>Bhuvanasundarī</s> one should worship <s>Tryambaka</s>.

children.text: svarge martye ca pātāle yā cādyā bhuvaneśvarī
children.translated_text: She who is the primordial <s>Bhuvaneśvarī</s> in heaven, on earth, and in the underworlds,
because <s>Tryambaka</s> delights among these, he is so called.
He is described as accompanied by his Śakti and is worshipped in all tantras.
On the right side of <s>Bhairavī</s> is the one named <s>Dakṣiṇāmūrti</s>.
With utmost care one should worship that very five-faced one.
On the right side of <s>Chinnamastā</s> one should worship <s>Śiva</s> as <s>Kabandha</s>.
By worshipping <s>Kabandha</s>, O Goddess, one becomes lord of all siddhis.
<s>Dhūmāvatī</s> is the great vidyā bearing the form of a widow.
On the right side of <s>Bagalā</s> one should worship the one-faced one,
famed as <s>Mahārudra</s>, the maker of the world's destruction.
On the right side of <s>Mātaṅgī</s> one should worship <s>Śiva</s> as <s>Mataṅga</s>,
that very <s>Dakṣiṇāmūrti</s>, whose form is the bliss of the world.
On the right side of <s>Kamalā</s>, <s>Sadāśiva</s> in the form of <s>Viṣṇu</s>

children.text: pūjayet parameśāni sa siddho nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be worshipped, O supreme Lady; he becomes accomplished, of this there is no doubt.
On the right side of <s>Annapūrṇā</s> one should worship the god in the form of <s>Brahmā</s>,
<s>Maheśvara</s>, ten-faced, who bestows great liberation.
In the region to the right of <s>Durgā</s> one should worship <s>Nārada</s>.

children.text: nākāraḥ sṛṣṭikartā ca dakāraḥ pālakaḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: The syllable na is the creator, and the syllable da is always the protector;
because the repha has the nature of destruction, he is called <s>Nārada</s>.
For all the other vidyās, whatever seer is traditionally stated,

children.text: sa eva tasyā bhartā ca dakṣabhāge prapūjayet
children.translated_text: he himself is her husband too, and should be worshipped on the right side.
The glorious Goddess said:

children.text: yā cādyā paramā vidyā dvitīyā bhairavī parā
children.translated_text: She who is the primordial supreme vidyā, and the second, the supreme <s>Bhairavī</s>,
the eternal mother of the three worlds: how is she borne by a corpse?
The glorious <s>Śiva</s> said:
She who is primordial, O supreme Lady, herself has Time as her form.
Established in the lotus of glorious <s>Śiva</s>'s heart, she has destruction as her form.
Therefore <s>Mahākāla</s> is the maker of the world's destruction.
When <s>Kālī</s>, whose form is destruction, is manifest in her own form,
then at once, O Goddess, <s>Sadāśiva</s> is in the form of a corpse.
At that very moment, restless-eyed one, that Goddess is borne by a corpse.
The glorious Goddess said:
If <s>Mahādeva</s> is in corpse-form, <s>Sadāśiva</s> is a dead body.

children.text: mṛtadehaṃ mahādeva salilaṃ vā kathaṃ nahi ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Mahādeva</s>, why is the dead body not water?
The glorious <s>Śiva</s> said:
In that state where <s>Mahākālī</s> is manifest, <s>Sadāśiva</s> is without Śakti.

children.text: śaktyā yukto yadā devi tadaiva śivarūpakaḥ
children.translated_text: When joined with Śakti, O Goddess, then indeed he has the form of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: śaktihīnaḥ śavaḥ sākṣāt puruṣatvaṃ na muñcati ||
children.translated_text: Without Śakti he is a corpse directly, though he does not give up his male nature.
The glorious <s>Śiva</s> said:
Listen, O Goddess; I shall briefly explain the essence of yoga.
The body is shaped like a tree, with its root above and branches below.

children.text: brahmāṇḍe yāni tīrthāni tāni santi kalevare
children.translated_text: Whatever sacred places exist in the macrocosm, those exist in the body.
The form that belongs to the great macrocosm is the same form in the small body.
In the macrocosm there are sacred places amounting to three and a half crores,
and seventy-two thousand are manifest, O you honored by heroes.

children.text: caturdaśaṃ tu tanmadhye tanmadhye tritayaṃ śubham
children.translated_text: Among them are fourteen, and within those is an auspicious triad.
Within that, O supreme Lady, is <s>Mahādhīrā</s>, giver of liberation.
That <s>Vāsukī</s>, the great Māyā, has the form of a serpent.
She has the shape of three and a half coils and dwells in the floor of the underworld.
O supreme Lady, listen respectfully, in order, to the seven heavens:

children.text: bhūrlokaṃ ca bhuvarlokaṃ svarlokaṃ mahasaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhūrloka</s>, <s>Bhuvarloka</s>, <s>Svarloka</s>, and likewise <s>Mahas</s>,
<s>Janaloka</s>, <s>Tapas</s>, and <s>Satyaloka</s>, beautiful-faced one.
This is the sevenfold heaven, O fair one; listen carefully to the underworld.

children.text: atalaṃ vitalaṃ caiva sutalaṃ ca talātalam
children.translated_text: <s>Atala</s>, <s>Vitala</s>, <s>Sutala</s>, and <s>Talātala</s>,
<s>Mahātala</s>, <s>Pātāla</s>, and beyond that <s>Rasātala</s>.
From <s>Rasātala</s> up to <s>Satya</s>, <s>Mahādhīrā</s> is established.
The nāḍī located in the middle of <s>Meru</s> is <s>Mahādhīrā</s>, giver of liberation.
In <s>Satyaloka</s> is great <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Śiva</s> called the cosmic egg.
To behold him, <s>Vāsukī</s> is always eager.
When <s>Vāsukī</s> has risen, piercing the six heavens,
then all rivers that go to the ocean become upward-flowing.

children.text: evaṃ krameṇa deveśi śarīre nāḍayaḥ sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: In this manner, O queen of gods, the nāḍīs are situated in the body.

children.text: iḍā ca piṅgalā caiva suṣumṇā madhyavartinī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Iḍā</s> and <s>Piṅgalā</s> are there, and <s>Suṣumṇā</s> stands in the middle.
If, O queen of gods, one fills the breath through the two nāḍīs,

children.text: tatastu prāṇamantreṇa kuṇḍalī ca kramaṃ caret ||
children.translated_text: then, by means of the prāṇa-mantra, <s>Kuṇḍalī</s> proceeds in sequence.
In the great thousand-spoked lotus, in the eternal and imperishable lotus,
<s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>, filled with trembling, should enter the eternal abode.
All the channels going down to the netherworld then become upward-flowing;
at that time, O <s>Devī</s>, one should contemplate the garland of letters.
With knowledge one should recite the root-mantra one hundred and eight times;
by that path the wise practitioner should bring it back again to the <s>mūlādhāra</s>.
There he should satisfy the deities of the six cakras with a stream of nectar.
Now I shall tell you another thing, beloved: the posture of <s>yonimudrā</s>.
Having sat upon the seat, the mantra-practitioner should face east or north;
with both hands he should make a firm binding of the two knees.
Keeping the body straight, O queen of the gods, he should bring the nose down to the knees.
With the mantra of breath, O queen of the gods, he should very carefully

children.text: pūrayet parameśāni kiṃcid vāyuṃ na recayet
children.translated_text: fill himself with air, O supreme lady, and should not exhale even a little.
Keeping the body straight, O supreme lady, he should make it inverted with effort.
By the very method stated before he should recite one hundred and eight times;
there he should satisfy the deities of the six cakras with a stream of nectar.
By that path he should bring it to the <s>mūlādhāra</s>, O fair-faced one.
Beloved, the posture of <s>yonimudrā</s> pacifies every disease.
Why say much, O <s>Devī</s>? It destroys even great illnesses.
Why say much, O <s>Devī</s>? It is the cause of enlivening the mantra.
This <s>mudrā</s> brings direct realization of the self and bestows great liberation.

children.text: śatavaktraṃ yadi bhavet tadā vaktuṃ na śakyate ||
children.translated_text: Even if one had a hundred mouths, it could not be described.
O queen of the gods, how then can I now speak of it with only five mouths?
Even one afflicted with leprosy becomes one having the form of <s>Kāmarūpa</s>.
The blessed <s>Devī</s> said:
O god of gods, great god, deliverer from the ocean of saṃsāra,
tell me the great <s>mudrā</s> called bound-yoni, O storehouse of compassion.
The blessed <s>Śiva</s> said:
Listen, O <s>Devī</s>; I shall briefly explain the bound-yoni.
Having sat upon the seat, the mantra-practitioner should face east or north.
O great lady, he should place the tip of his own liṅga in the anal opening;

children.text: śrotre caiva tathā netre nāsāyāṃ ca tato mukhe ||
children.translated_text: then, likewise, at the ears, the eyes, the nose, and the mouth,
O great lady, the wise practitioner should apply the thumbs and the others in order.
At the nose and at the mouth he should, with great care,

children.text: pūrayet parameśāni kiṃcid api na recayet
children.translated_text: fill himself with air, O supreme lady, and should not exhale even a little.
Having made sound directly manifest, he should contemplate the garland of letters.
The wise practitioner should recite the root-mantra one hundred and eight times;
with the mantra <s>so 'ham</s>, O queen of the gods, he should bring it by that path.
There he should satisfy the deities of the six cakras with a stream of nectar.
When it has been done, O great lady, I shall tell you its fruit, O sinless one.
The blessed <s>Pārvatī</s> said:
Speak, O <s>Īśāna</s>, omniscient one, best of those who know all principles.
O lord of gods, tell the exceedingly rare mantra-path of <s>Kālikā</s>.
The blessed <s>Śiva</s> said:
Listen, O <s>Devī</s>, ever-blissful one, to the supreme mantra of <s>Kālikā</s>,
by the mere occasion of which a man becomes liberated while living.
It begins with <s>Śiva</s>, is furnished with bindu and nāda, and is joined with the left eye and fire;

children.text: siddhavidyā tv iyaṃ bhadre vidyārājñī sudurlabhā ||
children.translated_text: this, O gracious one, is the siddhavidyā, the queen of vidyās, very hard to obtain.
This first triad of seed-syllables is the sky adorned with bindu;
it is joined with the left ear. Now hear the other pair.
It is <s>Īśāna</s> joined with fire, and joined with the moon of the left eye;
this is the second, O supreme lady, and then comes the word of address.

children.text: punar bījatrayaṃ kūrcaṃ māyādvaṃdvaṃ ca ṭhadvayam
children.translated_text: Again there are the three seed-syllables, <s>kūrca</s>, the pair of <s>māyā</s>, and two <s>ṭha</s> syllables.
This twenty-two-syllabled mantra is the queen of vidyās, very hard to obtain.
The great vidyā beginning with <s>vāgbhava</s> has blessed <s>Kālī</s> as its deity;
the great vidyā beginning with <s>praṇava</s> has <s>Siddhikālikā</s> as its deity.
Two of its own seed-syllables, <s>kūrca</s>, and one seed-syllable, O supreme lady:

children.text: tryakṣarī paramā vidyā cāmuṇḍā kālikā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: the supreme three-syllabled vidyā is known as <s>Cāmuṇḍā Kālikā</s>.

children.text: etasyāḥ sadṛśī vidyā siddhidā nāsti sundari
children.translated_text: There is no vidyā like this one that grants siddhi, O beautiful one.

children.text: yathā ṣaḍakṣarī vidyā tathā vidyā ca tryakṣarī ||
children.translated_text: As is the six-syllabled vidyā, so also is the three-syllabled vidyā.
Its own three seed-syllables, O gracious one, then <s>Śmaśānakālikā</s>;
again the three seed-syllables, O gracious one, and one should utter the beloved of fire.
The fourteen-syllabled vidyā is worshipped in the three worlds.
<s>Dakṣiṇākālikā</s>, <s>Siddhakālikā</s>, <s>Guhyakālikā</s>,
<s>Śrīkālikā</s>, <s>Bhadrakālī</s>, supreme <s>Cāmuṇḍākālikā</s>,
<s>Śmaśānakālikā</s>, O <s>Devī</s>, and <s>Mahākālī</s>: thus it is eightfold.
Its own seed-syllable, O great lady, and then the word of address;
again the seed-syllable of <s>Kālikā</s>, and after that one should place the bride of fire.
Thus the eightfold mantra is concealed in all tantras.
The blessed <s>Devī</s> said:
I have heard the supremely secret mantra of <s>Mahākālikā</s>.
Now I wish to hear the king of mantras of <s>Tārā</s>,
by the mere occasion of which one does not sink in the ocean of becoming.

children.text: tanmantraṃ vada īśāna yadi sneho'sti māṃ prati
children.translated_text: Tell that mantra, O <s>Īśāna</s>, if you have affection for me.
The blessed <s>Śiva</s> said:
Having uttered the moon seed-syllable, the first one, combined with fire,
and joined with the moon of the left eye: this, beloved, is the king of mantras.
It is the one-syllabled great vidyā, worshipped in the three worlds.
Joined with the bindu of <s>Īśāna</s> and adorned with the left ear,
it is the one-syllabled great vidyā, the second king of mantras.
The head mounted with bindu, joined with the moon of the left eye,
the first seed-syllable and the second: one should utter the weapon-mantra.
When the vidyā begins with the <s>praṇava</s>, it is proclaimed as <s>Ugratārā</s>;
and the vidyā called <s>Ekajaṭā</s> is said to bestow great liberation.
Without the Tārā-weapon mantra, the three-syllabled one is Mahānīlasarasvatī;
when the vidyā begins with the Vāgbhava seed, it grants lordship over speech.
When the great vidyā begins with the Śrī seed, it always bestows Lakṣmī;
when the supreme vidyā begins with Māyā, it always grants accomplishment.
And this one, beginning with the Kūrca seed, reveals the aggregate of sound;
the great vidyā beginning with Gagana bestows nirvāṇa and liberation.
The great vidyā beginning with Prāsāda grants union with Śiva;
and this one beginning with the Prāṇa seed grants the accomplishment of desires.
The great vidyā beginning with Kālikā always gives liberation and accomplishment;
the worship of <s>Kālikā</s> and <s>Tārā</s> is now taught here.
Rising in the morning, the knower of mantra should worship the guru in the thousand-petalled lotus;
having pierced the six cakras, he should recite one hundred and eight times.
Then, having bowed according to rule, he should begin the act of bathing;
after uttering 'today' and the rest, he should state the solar month.
Thereafter, for the pleasure of the deity, he should bathe with pure water;

children.text: oṃkāraṃ ca samuccārya gaṅge ceti samuccaret ||
children.translated_text: uttering the syllable Oṃ, he should also recite 'O Gaṅgā' and so on.
Then he should say 'Yamunā,' and afterwards 'Godāvarī, Sarasvatī,'
and, saying 'Narmadā,' together with Sindhu and Kāverī.

children.text: asmin jale ca saṃnidhiṃ kuru śabdamatho vadet
children.translated_text: He should then say the words, 'be present in this water';
by means of the mudrā called the goad, he should draw them from the solar orb.
O goddess, he should display the four mudrās with great care;
covering it with the Fish-mudrā, he should recite the mantra eleven times.
Facing the sun, he should cast out water according to the number of the sun;
uttering the root mantra, he should wash both feet.
He should immerse himself three times in the water flowing from his feet and recite the mantra;

children.text: mūlamantraṃ trir japtvā tu mudrayā kumbhasaṃjñayā ||
children.translated_text: having recited the root mantra three times, with the mudrā known as the Jar,
rising from the water, O goddess of gods, he should apply the tilaka according to the Kaula path;
then he should sip water with milk, using the tattvas of self, vidyā, and Śiva.
Mantras joined with the fire-wife are to be understood as beginning with praṇava;
O goddess, with the formula beginning 'O Gaṅgā' he should perform the summoning of the tīrtha.

children.text: mūlena darbhayā bhūmau trivāraṃ nikṣipet sudhīḥ
children.translated_text: With the root mantra, the wise man should sprinkle it three times on the ground with darbha grass;
with that water he should perform self-consecration seven times.
Then, having performed the aṅganyāsa, on the left hand, O mistress of the gods,
he should place Gagana, the wind seed, Varuṇa, and the earth seed.
He should recite three times the fire seed furnished with bindu;
by this mantra, O goddess, that water is consecrated.
Uttering the root mantra seven times with the tattva-mudrā,
by the mere act of consecration he is freed from all sins.
The remaining water, O great lady, he should bring into his right hand;
he should fill the water through Iḍā and wash what is within the body.

children.text: tataḥ piṅgalayā devi tattoyaṃ tu virecayet
children.translated_text: Then, O goddess, he should expel that water through Piṅgalā;
he should imagine that black-colored water as the form of sin.
In front of him, upon a vajra-stone, he should cast it away with the cry phaṭ;
having washed his hands and sipped water, preceded by prāṇāyāma,
he should satisfy the family deity and offer arghya to the sun.
After that comes the deity's arghya and the supreme-syllabled Gāyatrī.

children.text: praṇavaṃ ca samuddhṛtya kālikāyai tato vadet
children.translated_text: Having first pronounced the praṇava, he should then say 'to Kālikā';

children.text: vidmahe iti saṃlikhya śmaśānaṃ ca samuddharet ||
children.translated_text: writing 'we know,' he should then pronounce 'cremation-ground.'

children.text: vāsinīṃ ṅeyutāṃ devi dhīmahīti tato vadet
children.translated_text: O goddess, he should say 'dwelling one,' joined with ṅe, and then say 'we meditate';
O dreadful great lady, he should recite 'may that one impel us.'
The wise man should recite the Gāyatrī and cast up water three times;
then he should recite the great mantra, the supreme-syllabled Gāyatrī.
Then, having performed the aṅganyāsa and having sipped water, O supreme lady,
O great lady, he should meditate on his chosen goddess within the circle.

children.text: oṃ tārāyai vidmahe iti mahogrāyai tato vadet
children.translated_text: 'Oṃ, may we know Tārā,' he should say, and then 'the very fierce one';
after that, he should say 'we meditate,' and then, O goddess, 'may she impel us.'
Then, having performed prāṇāyāma, he should recite one hundred and eight times.
O goddess of gods, the procedure of worship is taught here in thread-like outline.
Having carefully performed the auspicious recitation and resolve, and having set up the pot,
he should perform sipping of water with the mantra and then place the general arghya.
With that water he should sprinkle the doorway and perform the worship of the door;
having driven away the three kinds of obstacles, next comes the removal of spirits.

children.text: āsanaṃ ca samabhyarcya gurudevaṃ namet sudhīḥ
children.translated_text: Having duly worshipped the seat, the wise man should bow to the guru-deity;

children.text: karaśuddhiṃ ca tālaṃ ca trayaṃ digbandhanaṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: then come purification of the hands, the clapping rite, the threefold binding of the directions.
An enclosure with fire should be made, and then he should perform purification of the elements;
he should perform the six limbs of the Mātṛkā and the inner Mātṛkā rite.

children.text: mātṛkādhyānam uccārya bāhye tu mātṛkāṃ nyaset
children.translated_text: Having recited the meditation on Mātṛkā, he should place the external Mātṛkā;
then, having performed pīṭha-nyāsa, he should perform prāṇāyāma.
He should perform the ṛṣi and other nyāsas, the hand-and-limb nyāsa, and the letter nyāsa;
then, O goddess, the sixfold nyāsa, and after that the pervasive nyāsa.
Thus, with concentrated mind, he should perform tattva-nyāsa;

children.text: bījanyāsaṃ tato devi vyāpakaṃ vinyaset sudhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: then, O goddess, the wise man should place the seed-nyāsa and the pervasive nyāsa.

children.text: mūlena saptadhā dhyānaṃ mānasaiḥ pūjanaṃ caret
children.translated_text: With the root mantra he should perform meditation seven times and mental worship;
then the special arghya, worship of the pīṭha, renewed meditation together with the eye rite.
The display of mudrās and the rest should be done, along with invocation and the six-limbed rite;
then the Dhenu and other mudrās, the installation of life-breath, and worship with the root mantra.
He should worship the prayer for command, the limbs, and Kāli and the others;
he should worship Brāhmī and the others, Asitāṅga and the others, and Mahākāla.
He should again worship the swords and the rest, the line of gurus, and the goddess.

children.text: balidānaṃ tato homaṃ prāṇāyāmaṃ tato japam ||
children.translated_text: After that come the offering of bali, the homa, then prāṇāyāma, and then japa.
The wise man should dedicate the japa and then perform prāṇāyāma.
At this time, O Devī, he should gather the ritual substances and the rest.

children.text: arghyaṃ dattvā maheśāni cātmānaṃ ca samarpayet
children.translated_text: Having given arghya, O Maheśānī, he should also dedicate himself.

children.text: stutiṃ ca kavacaṃ smṛtvā cāṣṭāṅgaṃ praṇamet sudhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: Remembering the hymn and the kavaca, the wise man should bow down with the eight-limbed prostration.
Meditating, “I am Śiva,” he should dismiss the deity by the rite of withdrawal.
Having made a maṇḍala in the northeast, beginning with the leftovers of the Cāṇḍālī rite,

children.text: arghyaṃ saṃdhārya śirasi candanaṃ tu lalāṭake
children.translated_text: and having held arghya on his head and sandal paste on his forehead,
he should take a little of the naivedya and then move about according to his own wish.
Or the mantra-practitioner, composed in mind, may perform the abbreviated worship.
First comes the nyāsa beginning with the seer and the rest; after that, purification of the hands.
Then the finger-nyāsa and the pervasive nyāsa, and the nyāsa beginning with the heart.
Then the three claps, the sealing of the directions, and after that prāṇāyāma.
Meditation, mental sacrifice, and the setting down of the arghya follow.
He should perform the worship of the pīṭha, then meditation again, and then invocation.
After performing the jīva-nyāsa, he should worship the supreme deity.
He should worship the limbs, Kāli and the others, Brāhmī and the others, and the eight Bhairavas.
Having worshipped Mahākāla, he should then worship the line of gurus.
Having worshipped the swords and the rest, he should again worship the goddess.
Then, after performing prāṇāyāma, the foremost practitioner should worship.
He should then make the dedication of the fruit of the japa into the hand of the goddess.

children.text: prāṇāyāmaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā cāṣṭāṅgaṃ praṇamet sudhīḥ
children.translated_text: After performing prāṇāyāma, the wise man should bow down with the eight-limbed prostration.

children.text: stutiṃ ca kavacaṃ smṛtvā viśeṣārghyaṃ pradāpayet ||
children.translated_text: Remembering the hymn and the kavaca, he should offer the special arghya.
Having made the self-dedication, he should dismiss the deity by the rite of withdrawal.
Having made a maṇḍala in the northeast, beginning with the leftovers of the Cāṇḍālī rite,
he should take a little naivedya and then move about according to his own wish.
Devī said:
The worship of Kālikā has been heard; now tell me that of Tārā,
by the mere occasion of whom the speech of men becomes conscious and inspired.
Īśvara said:

children.text: śṛṇu cārvaṅgi subhage tārāyāḥ pūjanaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: Listen, O lovely-limbed, fortunate one, to the great worship of Tārā.
Having performed ācamana with the mantra, he should then bow to the guru-deity.

children.text: jalaṃ saṃśodhya hastau ca pādau ca kṣālayettataḥ
children.translated_text: He should purify the water and then wash his hands and feet.
Having performed ācamana with the mantra, he should then contemplate the pīṭha.

children.text: śikhāṃ baddhvā tato devi trividhaṃ vighnanāśanam
children.translated_text: Having tied the topknot, O Devī, he should next perform the threefold destruction of obstacles.

children.text: bhūmyāsanaṃ ca saṃśodhya vastre granthiṃ vidhāya ca ||
children.translated_text: He should purify the ground-seat and tie a knot in the cloth.
Having purified body and speech, he should then purify the flowers.

children.text: yantraṃ kṛtvā sādhakendraḥ sāmānyārghyaṃ ca vinyaset ||
children.translated_text: Having made the yantra, the chief practitioner should set down the general arghya.
After fully worshipping the door guardians, he should begin the worship of the pīṭha.
Then he should worship the pīṭha-śaktis, Lakṣmī and the others, and recite the pīṭha-mantra.
I shall teach the bhūtaśuddhi, the particular form that applies here.
With inhalation, O Sureśvarī, by means of the haṃsa joined with the kūrca,
the practitioner should make himself, together with Kuṇḍalī, into the form of the twenty-four seed-syllables.
There, O Deveśī, these are dissolved in the supreme self.
With Māyā he should burn the sinful man, black like lamp-soot.
The discerning man, O Varārohā, should make him ashes by retention of the breath.
With the bride-seed, O Deveśī, he should exhale him together with the ashes.
Then, with inhalation by the kūrca, he should visualize an accumulation of nectar on the forehead.
O Parameśānī, by retention of the breath he should visualize an ocean of nectar.

children.text: āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ vahnibījāntaṃ hṛdi caikādaśaṃ japet ||
children.translated_text: He should recite in the heart eleven times “āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ” ending with the fire-seed.
Then the wise man should visualize, from the syllable oṃ, a red lotus.
Above it he should again meditate on the syllable huṃ, dark-blue in appearance.
Above that he should again meditate on a knife adorned with seed-syllables.

children.text: tasyopari paraṃ binduṃ śivarūpaṃ ca avyayam ||
children.translated_text: Above that is the supreme bindu, imperishable and of the nature of Śiva.
The bindu, extremely difficult to obtain, is one thousandth part of a grain of sand.
Within the bindu is Maṇidvīpa, extending for a hundred yojanas.
Within the bindu is the supreme light, a sphere shaped like a bubble.
Just as, O Devī, one sees a reflection in a bubble,
so the observation should be made with the eye of knowledge.
Within it is Maṇidvīpa, made of golden sand.
The mantra-practitioner should visualize it all around, made charming by moats.
In the middle he should meditate on a wish-fulfilling tree and on himself as consisting of Tāriṇī.
He should contemplate the excellent disk of light, shining like the rising sun,
provided with four gates and adorned with golden ramparts.
It is beautifully adorned with many divine maidens bearing chowries, bells, and the like,
accompanied by a gentle wind and decorated with fragrance and incense.
In its center he should meditate on an altar adorned with various jewels.
He should contemplate an excellent parasol made with golden thread.
Beneath that, O beloved, the mantra-practitioner should contemplate a jeweled lion-throne.
There he should contemplate the goddess according to the prescribed yoga of meditation.
He should worship her with the offerings taught in the Yogasāra.
Then, having performed prāṇāyāma, he should perform the nyāsa beginning with the seer and the rest.
After performing the varṇa-nyāsa, he should perform the hand-and-limb nyāsa.
With finger-snaps he should perform the three claps and the binding of the ten directions.
Then, having performed the sixfold nyāsa, he should next perform the pervasive nyāsa.
Having set up the special arghya, he should purify the five tattvas.
Bringing in the nectar-goddess, he should perform the fivefold assimilation.

children.text: kumbhe puṣpaṃ samādāya trikoṇe triḥ prapūjayet ||
children.translated_text: Taking a flower in the pot, he should worship three times in the triangle.

children.text: vāmadehaṃ tridhā coktvā khecarīṃ daśadhā japet
children.translated_text: Having uttered the left-side formula threefold, he should recite <s>Khecarī</s> ten times,

children.text: tathā cānandagāyatrīm ṛcaṃ ca trir japet sudhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: and likewise the <s>Ānandagāyatrī</s> and the ṛc three times, if he is wise.
O <s>Sureśvarī</s>, the curse of <s>Brahmā</s>, the curse of <s>Śukra</s>, and the curse of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>
the intelligent man should destroy by recitation in the quarters; then he should recite the three mantras.
The knife, the nectar, and also the protection of affection,

children.text: pāvamānaṃ ca trir japtvā śoṣaṇādīn samācaret ||
children.translated_text: and the <s>Pāvamāna</s> he should recite three times; then he should perform drying and the other acts.

children.text: vāruṇaṃ trir japeddevi cāmṛtaṃ saptadhā japet
children.translated_text: O goddess, he should recite the Varuṇa mantra three times, and recite the nectar mantra seven times.
In the vidyā-tattva, having displayed the cow-mudrā, he should recite the root mantra eight times.
Having raised <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>, he should then contemplate, 'I am <s>Śiva</s>.'
Having purified meat and fish, he should perform the purification of the mudrā-offering.

children.text: śaktiṃ ca kulapuṣpaṃ ca śodhayet sādhakottamaḥ
children.translated_text: The best of sādhakas should purify the śakti and the kula-flower,
and should satisfy the gods, the ancestors, the seers, and his chosen deity.
Taking the purified substance, he should place it in the special arghya.
Then, meditating that it is made of <s>Brahman</s>, he should perform the worship and meditation.

children.text: nāsārandhrāt samānīya pīṭhe puṣpaṃ nidhāya ca
children.translated_text: Drawing it through the nostril and placing the flower on the seat,
then, after making the invocation, he should display the five mudrās.
Having worshipped with the six limbs, he should display the mudrā again.
Then, having performed the life-nyāsa, he should worship with the offerings.
Having worshipped the six limbs, he should worship <s>Akṣobhya</s> below.
Having worshipped the line of gurus, he should worship at the ten roots.
He should worship <s>Kālī</s> and the others preceded by 'great', and <s>Vairocana</s> and the others.
Then, after worshipping the goddess again, the discerning man should give the bali offering.
After that, having performed prāṇāyāma, he should undertake meditation on the mantra.

children.text: japaṃ kṛtvā maheśāni devyā haste samarpayet ||
children.translated_text: Having made the recitation, O <s>Maheśānī</s>, he should offer it into the goddess's hand.
Having performed prāṇāyāma again, he should undertake the acceptance of the tattvas.

children.text: tasmai dattvā svayaṃ nītvā prajapet sādhakāgraṇīḥ ||
children.translated_text: Giving it to him and taking it himself, the foremost sādhaka should recite.

children.text: pītvā pītvā japitvā ca muktaḥ koṭijanaiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Drinking again and again and reciting, he is liberated together with ten million people.
At each vessel the wise man should recite the mantra one hundred and eight times.

children.text: stutiṃ ca kavacaṃ smṛtvā cāṣṭāṅgaṃ praṇamet sudhīḥ
children.translated_text: Remembering the hymn and the armor, the wise man should bow with the eight limbs.
The special arghya is to be given, and he should surrender himself.
Having himself become Rudra-formed, he should dismiss the deity by the rite of dissolution.
Then, having bound the yoni-mudrā, he should dismiss her, saying, 'Forgive me.'
O <s>Maheśānī</s>, after the limb-nyāsa comes prāṇāyāma.
Making a maṇḍala in the northeast, he should worship with the remnants of worship.
With 'ṅe' at the end: 'Again and again homage to <s>Caṇḍeśvarī</s>, who dwells in the remnants.'

children.text: nirmālyaṃ dhārayet śīrṣe candanaṃ ca lalāṭake ||
children.translated_text: He should place the remnant on his head, and sandal paste on his forehead.

children.text: gurusthāne likhed yantraṃ vicared bhairavo yathā
children.translated_text: He should draw the yantra at the guru's place and move about like <s>Bhairava</s>.
O goddess, the concise worship is mental and devoid of the tattvas.
The wise man should perform here what has been taught here, and should not introduce anything else.
O goddess, through introducing anything else, <s>Tāriṇī</s> becomes angry.

children.text: tattvajñānaṃ ca mānaṃ ca śaktimātre hi pārvati
children.translated_text: O <s>Pārvatī</s>, knowledge of the tattvas and the measure belong only to the śakti.
Thus this has been told, O goddess. What else do you wish to hear?
The blessed goddess said:
By your grace, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, I am purified, and not otherwise.
O god, I now wish to hear the worship of <s>Śambhunātha</s>.
<s>Śiva</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇu pārvati vakṣyāmi yanmāṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi
children.translated_text: Listen, O <s>Pārvatī</s>; I shall explain what you ask me.
Having extracted <s>Nakulīśa</s>, adorned with the anusvāra,
joined with bindu, nāda, and kalā, the great mantra called <s>Prāsāda</s>
has had its greatness declared by me in the upper transmission.
Having extracted the salutation, ending in 'va' and adorned with the eye,
with the Varuṇa syllable, the mouth-circle, and the wind joined with the forehead,
this is the five-syllabled mantra, bestowing the fruit of the five transmissions.

children.text: praṇavādi yadā devi tadā mantraṃ ṣaḍakṣaram ||
children.translated_text: When, O goddess, it begins with praṇava, then the mantra is six-syllabled.
Having extracted the mantra called <s>Prāsāda</s>, and then 'to <s>Ardhanārīśvara</s>',
and again having extracted <s>Prāsāda</s>, this is a mantra to be most deeply concealed.
O daughter of the mountain, my form is thus of many kinds.

children.text: kaṇṭhe tu garalaṃ devi na kalau bhāvayet kvacit ||
children.translated_text: But, O goddess, in the Kali age one should never contemplate poison in my throat.
If one desires one's own death, if one desires madness,
only then, O goddess, do people rashly worship <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s>.
O goddess, if by the force of bad fortune one composes a hymn and the like to <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s>,

children.text: karoti kārayedvāpi mama hatyāṃ karoti saḥ ||
children.translated_text: or causes another to do so, he commits my murder.

children.text: ata eva maheśāni sa pāpiṣṭho na cānyathā
children.translated_text: For that very reason, O <s>Maheśānī</s>, he is the worst sinner; it is not otherwise.
If a foolish man commits the sin of forbidden practice,
his sons, wives, and wealth come to destruction, without doubt.

children.text: kaṇṭhe tu garalaṃ devi yadi pūjāparo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: O goddess, if one becomes intent on worship with poison in the throat,
in this world he becomes poor, and after death he goes to the state of a pig.
If one performs preparatory rites for the mantra of <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s>,
within a fortnight, O <s>Maheśānī</s>, his death occurs, and not otherwise.
Listen, O goddess; I shall explain the worship of <s>Śiva</s> with an earthen image.
There, at the beginning, O <s>Parameśānī</s>, the wise man should bow to the guru-deity.
With 'oṃ, homage to <s>Hara</s>,' the wise man should bring clay.
With 'homage to <s>Maheśvara</s>,' he should carefully fashion the liṅga.
Uttering '<s>Śūlapāṇi</s>, be well established here,'
by this mantra, O goddess, the life-nyāsa is prescribed.
The syllable śa, joined with bindu, pronounced long, is the six-limbed formula.
I shall explain its meditation; listen with full attention.

children.text: oṃ dhyāyennityaṃ maheśaṃ rajatagirinibhaṃ cārucandrāvataṃsaṃ ratnākalpojjvalāṅgaṃ paraśumṛgavarābhītihastaṃ prasannam
children.translated_text: One should always meditate on <s>Maheśa</s>, resembling a silver mountain, wearing the beautiful moon as an ornament, his limbs shining with jewel ornaments, gracious, with hands holding an axe and a deer and granting boons and fearlessness.

children.text: padmāsīnaṃ samantāt stutam amaragaṇair vyāghrakṛttiṃ vasānaṃ viśvādyaṃ viśvabījaṃ nikhilabhayaharaṃ pañcavaktraṃ trinetram ||
children.translated_text: Seated on a lotus, praised on all sides by hosts of immortals, wearing a tiger skin, the source of the universe, the seed of the universe, remover of all fear, five-faced and three-eyed.

children.text: puṣpaṃ śirasi saṃdhārya mānasaiḥ pūjanaṃ caret
children.translated_text: Having placed a flower on his head, he should perform worship mentally.

children.text: punardhyātvā maheśāni śive puṣpaṃ nidhāya ca ||
children.translated_text: Then, having meditated again, O <s>Maheśānī</s>, he should place the flower on <s>Śiva</s>.
And, uttering "the bearer of <s>Pināka</s>," he should say twice, "come here."

children.text: iha tiṣṭha tato dvaṃdvaṃ saṃnidhehi dvayam iha ||
children.translated_text: Then he should say the pair, "stay here," and twice, "be present here."

children.text: iha sanni tato ruddhasvaśabdaṃ ca tato vadet
children.translated_text: Then, after "be present here," he should say the word "be restrained" with its own sound.
Having uttered "as long as the worship," he should then say, "so I perform."

children.text: snānīyaṃ ca paśupatiṃ ṅeyuktaṃ ca namaścaret
children.translated_text: For the bathing water he should make obeisance to <s>Paśupati</s>, joined with ṅe.
O goddess, the excellent brahmin practitioner should join it with what begins with the Veda.
O <s>Maheśānī</s>, saying "this is water for washing the feet," and then the six-syllabled mantra,
and uttering the salutation, the discerning man should offer everything.
Having worshipped <s>Maheśa</s>, O <s>Maheśānī</s>, he should worship the eight-formed one.

children.text: śarvo bhavastathā rudra ugro bhīmaḥ paśoḥ patiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śarva</s>, <s>Bhava</s>, likewise <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Ugra</s>, <s>Bhīma</s>, and <s>Paśupati</s>,

children.text: mahādevaṃ ca īśānaṃ ṅeyutaṃ kuru yatnataḥ
children.translated_text: and <s>Mahādeva</s> and <s>Īśāna</s>: carefully make each joined with ṅe.

children.text: kṣitiṃ jalaṃ tathā cāgniṃ vāyuṃ cākāśameva ca ||
children.translated_text: Earth, water, likewise fire, wind, and space,

children.text: yajamānaṃ tathā somaṃ sūryaṃ ca mūrtinā saha
children.translated_text: and the sacrificer, the moon, and the sun, together with the corresponding form:
having made each joined with ṅe everywhere, the best practitioner should worship.
He should worship counterclockwise, beginning with praṇava and ending with namaḥ.
These are the eight forms of <s>Śiva</s>, in order beginning with the east.
After worshipping up to the southeast, he should worship the vidyā and <s>Liṅgiśiva</s>.
Then he should recite one thousand and eight times, or one hundred times.
"You are the protector of what is secret and more than secret; accept this recitation made by us.
May success be mine, O god, through your grace, O <s>Maheśvara</s>."
Then, taking water, he should offer the recitation itself.

children.text: mukhavādyaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā cāṣṭāṅgaṃ praṇamet sudhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, having made mouth-music, the wise man should bow with the eight limbs.
By the rite of dissolution he should dismiss <s>Mahādeva</s>, saying, "Forgive me."

children.text: evaṃ pūjā prakartavyā śaktimantrān yajed yadi ||
children.translated_text: In this way worship is to be performed if one worships the śakti-mantras.
If one is intent on initiation into the great mantras beginning with <s>Prāsāda</s>,
śakti-initiation should never be performed out of delusion.

children.text: sa śaiva iti vikhyātaḥ sarvatantreśvaro bhavet
children.translated_text: He is famed as a Śaiva and becomes lord over all tantras.
Now then I shall teach the sūtra that is supremely secret.
<s>Hara</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, <s>Śūlapāṇi</s>, bearer of <s>Pināka</s>,
<s>Paśupati</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, and <s>Mahādeva</s>, in this order:
then, O goddess, the excellent practitioner should worship the eight forms.
Then, O <s>Maheśānī</s>, he should recite, and after that perform mouth-music.
Nothing other than this should be done if one is intent on śakti-initiation.
Because of performing what is forbidden, O goddess, a man becomes a sharer in sin.
O <s>Mahādevī</s>, if he performs worship and the like deficiently or excessively,

children.text: sa guruṃ cāpi śiṣyaṃ ca śivahatyāṃ prayacchati ||
children.translated_text: he brings upon the guru and also the disciple the killing of <s>Śiva</s>.
O <s>Maheśānī</s>, if even a single syllable is deficient or excessive,
in the number of phonemes, O <s>Maheśānī</s>, there will be the sin of brahmin-murder.

children.text: ata eva sa pāpiṣṭhaḥ satyaṃ satyaṃ sureśvari
children.translated_text: Therefore he is indeed the most sinful; true, true, O queen of the gods.
Having first performed worship in this way, then he should worship another.

children.text: ādau śivaṃ pūjayitvā śaktipūjā tataḥ param
children.translated_text: Having worshipped <s>Śiva</s> first, worship of Śakti comes afterward.

children.text: yat kiṃcid upacāraṃ hi tasya kiṃcinnivedayet ||
children.translated_text: Whatever service-offering there is, he should offer some part of it to him.

children.text: anyathā mūtravat sarvaṃ gaṅgātoyaṃ bhaved yadi
children.translated_text: Otherwise everything, even if it were water from the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, would become like urine.

children.text: ata eva maheśāni ādau liṅgaṃ prapūjayet ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, O <s>Maheśānī</s>, he should worship the liṅga first.
O goddess, if he places the water from <s>Śiva</s>'s bath on his head,

children.text: satyaṃ satyaṃ maheśāni śivatulyo na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: true, true, O <s>Maheśānī</s>, he is equal to <s>Śiva</s>; there is no doubt.
Having himself become of the form of <s>Śiva</s>, he should perform the worship of the goddess.
Whether initiated as a Śaiva, Vaiṣṇava, Daurga, Ārka, Gāṇapatya, or Aindra,

children.text: ādau liṅgaṃ pūjayitvā yadi cānyat prapūjayet
children.translated_text: if he first worships the liṅga and then worships another deity,

children.text: tatphalaṃ koṭiguṇitaṃ satyaṃ satyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the fruit of that is multiplied ten million times; true, true, there is no doubt.

children.text: anyadevaṃ pūjayitvā śivaṃ paścād yajed yadi
children.translated_text: But if he worships another deity and afterward worships <s>Śiva</s>,
the fruit of his worship is consumed by yakṣas and rākṣasas.

children.text: iti te kathitaṃ kānte tantrāṇāṃ sāramuttamam
children.translated_text: Thus, O beloved, I have taught you the highest essence of the tantras.

children.text: bahu kiṃ kathyate devi bhūyaḥ kiṃ śrotumicchasi ||
children.translated_text: Why say much, O goddess? What more do you wish to hear?
The blessed goddess said:
I have heard the supremely secret mantra of <s>Mahākālikā</s>.

children.text: saṃkṣepaṃ kathitaṃ nātha vāsanāṃ vada māṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: You have told it briefly, O lord; tell me its vāsanā.
Blessed <s>Śiva</s> said:
Listen, O goddess, to the vāsanā of the great mantra, which grants all attainments,

children.text: yasyāḥ śravaṇamātreṇa mantrāḥ siddhā bhavanti hi ||
children.translated_text: by merely hearing which mantras become perfected.
In the upper angles of the syllable ka, prāṇa, the vital wind, is established.
Apāna is in the wind-corner, and samāna is in the middle region.

children.text: udāno 'ṅkuśakoṇe ca mātrāyāṃ vyāna eva ca
children.translated_text: Udāna is in the goad-corner, and vyāna is in the mātrā.

children.text: bījaṃ tu kālikārūpaṃ prakāraṃ śṛṇu pārvati ||
children.translated_text: The seed is the form of <s>Kālikā</s>; listen to the procedure, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
In the kalā-section are the matted locks and the hair, O <s>Parameśvarī</s>.

children.text: bindumastakabhālaṃ tu nāsā netraṃ ca pārvati ||
children.translated_text: The bindu is the head and forehead, and the nose and eye, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
Likewise the pair of ears, the mouth, and what is arranged from the shoulders,
the four arms, the body, the pair of breasts, and the two hips,

children.text: hṛdayaṃ jaṭharaṃ pādaṃ tathā sarvāṅguliḥ śive
children.translated_text: the heart, belly, feet, and all the fingers and toes, O <s>Śivā</s>.
The syllable ka is Brahmā-form and the whole body; there is no doubt.

children.text: śakāraṃ kāmarūpaṃ ca yonirūpaṃ na cānyathā
children.translated_text: The syllable śa is desire-form and yoni-form, and not otherwise.
And the repha, having the form of moon, sun, and fire, is exceedingly rare.
It is the brilliance that illuminates all the limbs, having the form of the world's bliss.
It is the nāda that gives bindu and nirvāṇa, always granting great liberation.
O goddess, the syllable ka, water-formed, removes every obstacle.
The repha removes all sins; therefore it is fire, and not otherwise.
O <s>Parameśānī</s>, the syllable ī is śakti, whose form is imperishable.
The goddess grants great liberation; therefore she is proclaimed to be māyā.
The syllable ka has the form of <s>Brahmā</s>, and the syllable ma has the form of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Because the repha has the nature of dissolution, it is <s>Śiva</s>-formed, and not otherwise.
O <s>Parameśvarī</s>, the syllable ka is directly <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>.
O <s>Śivā</s>, without being joined with māyā, that very syllable would be unutterable.

children.text: māyāyuktaṃ yadā devi tadā muktipradaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: O goddess, when it is joined with māyā, then it is great and bestows liberation.
For this very reason, O <s>Maheśānī</s>, it is called the māyā-śakti.
O goddess, the syllable ka gives dharma, and the syllable ī gives artha.
O beloved, the syllable ra gives kāma, and the syllable ma gives mokṣa.
O goddess, when uttered together, it bestows nirvāṇa and liberation.

children.text: māhātmyaṃ devadeveśi kiṃ vaktuṃ śakyate mayā ||
children.translated_text: O mistress of the gods, how can its greatness be spoken by me?
With a thousand crores of tongues and with a hundred crores of mouths,
even over a thousand other births, it cannot be described.
Japa of one lakh according to rule is called puraścaraṇa.
O beautiful one, this is the form of the great Māyā, the kūrca-bīja.

children.text: vāgbhavaṃ praṇavaṃ devi etadrūpaṃ na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: O goddess, vāgbhava and praṇava have this form; there is no doubt.
The fire-born great vidyā has this form; there is no doubt.
The vidyā that quickly grants accomplishment is fire-born, the supreme mantra.
By the word of address alone she always brings about nearness.
Now I shall explain the excellent puraścaraṇa of the mahāvidyā.
The threefold puraścaraṇa of the king of mantras has been taught; listen.
By day one should recite the mantra one lakh times, eating sacrificial food and having conquered the senses.

children.text: divyavīramate devi rātrau lakṣaṃ japet sudhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: O goddess, according to the divine and heroic doctrine, the wise man should recite one lakh times at night.
Now listen, O goddess, to the preliminary rite of this six-syllabled mantra.
O <s>Pārvatī</s>, according to the divine and heroic doctrine, with twenty-one repetitions,

children.text: tathā ca tryakṣaraṃ mantraṃ prajapet sādhakāgraṇīḥ
children.translated_text: the foremost sādhaka should likewise recite the three-syllabled mantra.
Meditation, worship, and all the rest are the same, O you honored by heroes.

children.text: etasyāḥ sadṛśī vidyā phaladā nāsti yogini
children.translated_text: O yoginī, there is no vidyā like this one for granting fruit.
O <s>Pārvatī</s>, listen reverently to the consciousness of every mantra.
In the great lotus of the sahasrāra is supreme <s>Śiva</s> in the form of bindu.
The wise man, having raised kuṇḍalinī by the haṃsa-mantra,
O <s>Parameśvarī</s>, when a steady gaze arises at the tip of the nose,
then the mantra-consciousness comes to be in the kuṇḍalī-cakra.
In the great lotus of the sahasrāra, together with kuṇḍalinī,
one should visualize the guru; then, beloved, the consciousness of all mantras arises.
Only then should he recite the mantra, which grants accomplishment; of this there is no doubt.
The blessed goddess said:
Now tell me, O <s>Śaṃkara</s>, the vāsanā of the <s>Tāriṇī</s> mantra.
<s>Kālikā</s> is the giver of liberation, eternal, and <s>Tāriṇī</s> in the ocean of becoming.
Blessed <s>Śaṃkara</s> said:
O <s>Maheśānī</s>, the lord of kalās, described with bindu as his head,

children.text: nādaṃ ca vaktraṃ bhālaṃ ca nāsāṃ netraṃ ca pārvati ||
children.translated_text: and the nāda as mouth, forehead, nose, and eye, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
The four arms, the body, the pair of breasts, and the chest,

children.text: makāreṇa tu deveśi pṛṣṭhaṃ caiva kaṭidvayam ||
children.translated_text: and, O queen of gods, with the syllable ma, the back and the two hips.
With the syllable ta, the region of the womb, the anus, and the two feet likewise,
and all the fingers and nails: the best sādhaka should visualize them.
The repha, made of moon and sun, is the fire-bīja, and not otherwise.

children.text: sarvā nāḍyastathā jyotī romaṃ ca bhūṣaṇādikam ||
children.translated_text: All the nāḍīs likewise are light, and the hairs and ornaments and so on.
The syllable śa is the great Māyā, revealing herself as śakti.
From the head down to the feet, the śakti-bīja is very difficult to obtain.

children.text: asya mantrasya māhātmyaṃ kiṃ mayā kathyate'dhunā
children.translated_text: How can the greatness of this mantra be told by me now?
Thousands of horse sacrifices and hundreds of vājapeya rites,
O queen of gods, the sacred places such as <s>Kāśī</s>, comprising one and a quarter crore worlds,
O queen of gods, the earth with its seven continents, filled with grain,
gold equal to <s>Meru</s>, given to a brāhmaṇa learned in the Veda,
every vow with its proper fee, extensively including the four Vedas,

children.text: gāṃ caiva bhūmisaṃsthaṃ ca hastyaśvaṃ ca tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: cows, land, elephants, horses, and likewise
the offering of bali, O <s>Maheśānī</s>, and the sacrifice to the ancestors,
and whatever great merit is prescribed and spoken of by those who know scripture,
do not equal even a sixteenth part of a single recitation, O <s>Maheśānī</s>.
With one utterance, O queen of gods, what need is there to speak of pure brahman?
They are the agents of creation, maintenance, dissolution, and the rest; there is no doubt.

children.text: saguṇaṃ nirguṇaṃ sākṣāt nirākāraṃ ca mūrtimat
children.translated_text: It is with qualities and without qualities, directly formless and also embodied.
The great vidyā is in the sphere of vaikhārī speech, resting firmly on letters.
Because the reality is without syllables, therefore it is proclaimed as <s>Tārā</s>.
This has the nature of brahmavidyā and grants the fruits of enjoyment and liberation.
It cannot be described even in a thousand crores of births.
O queen of gods, even with five mouths, how can it now be told by me?
The one-syllabled mahāvidyā is worshiped in the three worlds.
O <s>Pārvatī</s>, one who receives a mantra without the one-syllabled vidyā,
for him accomplishment does not arise even in a thousand crores of kalpas.
The syllable sa has the form of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and the syllable ta is <s>Prajāpati</s>.
Because the repha has the nature of dissolution, it is directly <s>Śiva</s>; there is no doubt.

children.text: yā cādyā paramā vidyā sā māyā paramā kalā ||
children.translated_text: And that primordial, supreme vidyā is māyā, the supreme kalā.
It is formless, the supreme light, and the bindu called imperishable;

children.text: binduśabdena śūnyaṃ syāt tathā ca guṇasūcakam ||
children.translated_text: by the word bindu there is emptiness, and likewise it indicates the guṇas.
O goddess, the nectar of the bindu-cakra flows by means of the half-mora;
the nāda, whose form is the half-mora, is all-pervading and the protector of the universe.

children.text: yatheyaṃ vaikharī vidyā kūrcavidyā tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Just as this is the vaikharī vidyā, so too is the kūrca-vidyā;

children.text: māhātmyaṃ caiva pūjāyāṃ bhedo nāsti sureśvari ||
children.translated_text: in greatness and in worship there is no difference, O queen of the gods.

children.text: satāraṃ ca tathā binduṃ māyā pañcākṣarī parā
children.translated_text: Together with the tārā, and likewise the bindu, the māyā, and the supreme five-syllabled one,
when the syllables have been divided, the conception of the embodied form is made.
The vidyā of five and a half syllables, <s>Tāriṇī</s>, is herself embodied;
her form is indeed bird-shaped, and the vāgbhava belongs to <s>Haripriyā</s>.

children.text: praṇavaṃ kāmabījaṃ tu gaganaś ca śivaṃ śive
children.translated_text: The praṇava and the kāma-bīja, the sky, and <s>Śiva</s>, O <s>Śivā</s>,
that same is the weapon-bīja in the fire-born one, O queen of the gods.
By the word of address alone she always causes her presence;
with the five-syllabled mantra, O queen of gods, <s>Tāriṇī</s> is desire-formed.
Likewise, see the five-syllabled mantra as consisting of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>,
having the form of śakti, formless, and likewise through the five syllables.

children.text: yathā pañcākṣarī vidyā tathā vidyā ṣaḍakṣarī
children.translated_text: As is the five-syllabled vidyā, so is the six-syllabled vidyā;

children.text: tathaiva ṣoḍaśī vidyā tathā vidyā ca vyakṣarī ||
children.translated_text: so too is the sixteen-syllabled vidyā, and so too is the three-syllabled vidyā.
So too is the eight-syllabled vidyā, and so too is the supreme nine-syllabled one;
in greatness, meditation, and worship there is no difference, O queen of the gods.

children.text: atisnehena deveśi kiṃ mayā na prakāśitam
children.translated_text: Out of great affection, O queen of gods, what has not been revealed by me?
Even at the end of one's life one should not reveal the vaikharī before a paśu.
The blessed goddess said:
The goddess is full of great yoga, khecarī, the supreme kalā;
without yogic knowledge there is no accomplishment. This is true, O lord of the gods.
Tell me, O god of gods, from within the small brahmāṇḍa:
on what support, O lord, does the earth with its seven continents stand?
O lord, what form do the seven oceans have as their foundation?
In the mūlādhāra, in the earth-cakra, humans and the rest are established.
All people, of small form, are established in what shape?
Tell me of the wind according to the measure of one's own finger, O lord.
<s>Śiva</s> said:
O goddess, in the mūlādhāra the earth with its seven continents is situated;
the seven oceans are arranged in the form of rings.
<s>Jambudvīpa</s> is in the middle region, and outside it is the salt ocean;
O <s>Maheśānī</s>, there is <s>Śākadvīpa</s>, and outside that is the ocean of curds.
Outside that is <s>Śālmalīdvīpa</s>, and outside that is the ocean of milk;
outside that is <s>Pāṭalādvīpa</s>, and outside that is the water-ending ocean.
O goddess, whatever form humans and the rest have on the earth,

children.text: tena rūpeṇa deveśi mūlādhāre tu jantavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in that same form, O queen of gods, living beings are in the mūlādhāra.
O goddess, the wind is proclaimed to be ninety-six fingers in measure;
the measure of the sun's position is proclaimed to be greater.
The blessed goddess said:

children.text: kiyad bhuvaṃ tu brahmāṇḍaṃ vada bhūtalavāsinaḥ
children.translated_text: Tell me how much the earth and the brahmāṇḍa are for those who dwell on the ground.
What is the measure by one finger? Tell me, O treasury of compassion.
<s>Śiva</s> said:
By one finger, O queen of gods, one thousand years are produced;
for those who dwell on the ground it is ninety-six thousand years.
From the big toe up to the ankle, my dear, there are a thousand openings;
each opening is a thousand lunar years, from the ankle up to the knee-joints.
From the knees up to the anus, the measure is twenty thousand;
from the mūlādhāra up to the liṅga it is four thousand years.
From the liṅga up to the navel it is a thousand seers;
and from the navel up to the heart it is a thousand times the number of planets.
From the heart up to the throat it is a thousand times the number of seers;
from the viśuddha up to the ājñā the measure is a thousand times the number of Rudras.
From the ājñā-cakra up to <s>Śiva</s>, O queen of the gods, it is ten thousand;
the wind is remembered as a thousand times the number of suns, and greater still.
With the support of the body, contraction and increase arise;
it is sixfold at the time of sexual union, and threefold after eating.

children.text: dhamane cāṣṭadhā proktaḥ samīro vṛddhitāṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: In blowing it is said to be eightfold; the wind has entered a state of increase.
By the instruction of the true guru, through the path of mantra, O <s>Pārvatī</s>,

children.text: yadi caikāṅgulaṃ hrasvaṃ sahasrābdaṃ sa jīvati
children.translated_text: if it is shortened by one finger, he lives for a thousand years.

children.text: evaṃ krameṇa deveśi samatā yadi vā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: In this way, step by step, O queen of gods, if equality should come about,

children.text: jitvā mṛtyuṃ maheśāni śambhuvad viharet kṣitau
children.translated_text: having conquered death, O <s>Maheśānī</s>, he moves about on earth like <s>Śambhu</s>.
For that very reason, O <s>Maheśānī</s>, the yoni-mudrā has been taught by me.
By prāṇāyāma, O queen of gods, and likewise by the yoni-mudrā,
and likewise by the yoga of practice, if the wind becomes even,
having conquered death, O <s>Maheśānī</s>, he quickly becomes a khecara.
The whole measure of a human being has been told, O pleasant-speaking one.
Through the expansion of inhalation and exhalation, Kuṇḍalī moves in the sky.
The blessed goddess said:
Now tell me the measure of the earth, O <s>Parameśvara</s>.

children.text: saptasvargasthito yo yo yā yā śaktiḥ sthitā sadā
children.translated_text: Whatever śakti is always situated in each of the seven heavens,

children.text: tatsarvaṃ śrotumicchāmi yadi sneho'sti māṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: all that I wish to hear, if there is affection for me.
<s>Śiva</s> said:
In the mūlādhāra, in the earth-cakra, humans and the rest are established;

children.text: teṣāṃ mānena deveśi cārdhaṃ caiva dvisaptatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: by their measure, O queen of gods, it is half of seventy-two.
Outside that, O <s>Parameśānī</s>, the salt ocean is twice as large;
in this way, step by step, O queen of gods, it is proclaimed to be doubled.
O beautiful one, <s>Brahmā</s> together with <s>Ḍākinī</s> is in the mūlādhāra;
<s>Viṣṇu</s> together with <s>Rākiṇī</s> is established in the svādhiṣṭhāna.
<s>Rudra</s> together with <s>Lākinī</s> is in the maṇipūra, O queen of the gods.
In the great lotus of the anāhata, <s>Hara</s> is together with <s>Kākinī</s>.
In the one called viśuddha, <s>Sākinī</s> and <s>Sadāśiva</s> always dwell.
In the ājñā-cakra, O queen of the gods, are <s>Hākinī</s> and the god <s>Paraśiva</s>.
In the thousand-petalled great lotus is the supreme <s>Śiva</s>, whose form is the universe.
There the great <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s> stands eternally, O queen of the gods.
The blessed goddess said:
Where, at the root, is the great pīṭha situated, O supreme lord?
What is the underworld like below the mūlādhāra, O lord?
Blessed <s>Śiva</s> said:
In the mūlādhāra is <s>Kāmarūpa</s>; in the heart is <s>Jālaṃdhara</s>, my dear.
Below is <s>Pūrṇagiri</s>, and above that is <s>Uḍḍīyāna</s>.
<s>Vārāṇasī</s> is between the brows, and the blazing one is in the three eyes.
<s>Māyāvatī</s> is in the circle of the mouth, and <s>Aṣṭapurī</s> likewise in the throat.
At the root of the navel, O <s>Maheśānī</s>, the city of <s>Ayodhyā</s> is established.
The <s>Kāñcī</s> pīṭha is at the region of the hips, and <s>Śrīhṛṭṭa</s> at the region of the back.
One hundred from the mūlādhāra is declared to be <s>Atala</s>.
<s>Sutala</s> is one hundred years, and <s>Talātala</s> is one hundred, my dear.
<s>Mahātala</s> is established up to the number expressed by ṛṣi, arrow, and moon.
<s>Pātāla</s> extends to two hundred, and <s>Rasātala</s> indeed to two hundred.
And, O goddess of gods, two finger-breadths near the mūlādhāra are situated.
Between those two, O supreme goddess, the pātālas stand.

children.text: iti te kathitaṃ kānte yogasāraṃ samāsataḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, beloved, I have told you the essence of yoga in brief.

children.text: na vaktavyaṃ paśor agre prāṇānte'pi kadācana ||
children.translated_text: It should never be spoken before a paśu, even at the end of one's life.
The blessed goddess said:
The body is the abode of thirty-five million nāḍīs.

children.text: krameṇa śrotum icchāmi tad vadasva mayi prabho ||
children.translated_text: I wish to hear this in order; tell it to me, O lord.
Blessed <s>Śiva</s> said:
In the pores of the hairs, O beautiful one, there are twelve and a half million.
In the hands, mouth, and then the feet are nāḍīs numbered by fire and lakṣa.

children.text: udare ca tathā pāyau pañcalakṣāḥ prakīrtitāḥ
children.translated_text: In the belly and likewise in the anus, five lakhs are declared.
In the heart and all the limbs, nine lakhs are declared.

children.text: atha pārśve tathā carme tathaiva sarvasaṃdhiṣu
children.translated_text: Then in the sides, likewise in the skin, and similarly in all the joints,

children.text: rudrānnyūnaṃ sthitaṃ lakṣaṃ śarīre nāḍayaḥ priye ||
children.translated_text: there are a lakh less by eleven nāḍīs situated in the body, my dear.

children.text: iḍā ca piṅgalā caiva suṣumnā citriṇī tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Iḍā</s>, <s>Piṅgalā</s>, <s>Suṣumnā</s>, and <s>Citriṇī</s>,
and the <s>Brahmanāḍī</s> in their midst: these five nāḍīs are proclaimed.

children.text: kuhūś ca śaṅkhinī caiva gāndhārī hastijihvikā
children.translated_text: <s>Kuhū</s>, <s>Śaṅkhinī</s>, <s>Gāndhārī</s>, and <s>Hastijihvikā</s>,

children.text: nardinī ca tathā nidrā rudrasaṃkhyā vyavasthitā ||
children.translated_text: and likewise <s>Nardinī</s> and <s>Nidrā</s>: these are arranged in the number of Rudras.
These nāḍīs, O supreme lady, arise from the suṣumnā.
The blessed goddess said:
The numbers expressed by Vedas, eyes, Vasus, and apertures, and by arrows, water, and death,
on what support do they stand in the middle of the lotus, O supreme lord?
Blessed <s>Śiva</s> said:

children.text: yogapadmasya māhātmyaṃ mayā vaktuṃ na śakyate
children.translated_text: I am not able to state the greatness of the yoga-lotus.
In the middle of the lotus at the mūlādhāra is the very splendid seed-syllable laṃ.
In the middle of the bindu of the laṃ seed is the charming earth-cakra.
In the form of a circular enclosure, the seven oceans are situated.
The blessed goddess said:
Tell me the measure of the bindu, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, O lord.
Tell in order the measure of the yoga-lotus, O <s>Śaṃkara</s>.
Blessed <s>Śiva</s> said:
The bindu, very extensive, is one part of three parts of a paramāṇu.
Within it are all the oceans, the seven-islanded earth.

children.text: avyayaṃ paramaṃ sūkṣmaṃ bindurūpaṃ paraṃ śivam
children.translated_text: It is imperishable, supreme, subtle, the supreme <s>Śiva</s> in the form of bindu.

children.text: pramāṇaṃ cāsya devasya kiṃ vaktuṃ śakyate mayā ||
children.translated_text: How can I state the measure of this god?
O supreme lady, one should contemplate the world of <s>Brahmā</s> above the nāda.
There <s>Brahmā</s>, together with <s>Ḍākinī</s>, always dwells in the same way.
The syllable la is the earthy seed, O queen of the gods, in the form of śakti.
In the middle of the earth-cakra is the wondrous self-born liṅga.
It is always encircled by <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s> in the form of three and a half coils.
She remains covering the opening of the liṅga with her own mouth.
By that very means the breath always moves in <s>Iḍā</s> and <s>Piṅgalā</s>.
For the vision of the sahasrāra, she is always of the nature of wakefulness.
Whenever she rises through the path of <s>Brahman</s> to the sahasrāra,
then indeed, O supreme lady, there is the unfolding of inhalation and exhalation.

children.text: kesarasya tu madhye ca catuḥpattre sureśvari
children.translated_text: And in the middle of the filament, in the four-petalled lotus, O queen of the gods,
there are <s>Durgā</s> of infinite form and <s>Śambhu</s> bearing infinite forms.
They always abide with desire, in the play of manifold pleasures.
The blessed goddess said:
How does <s>Kuṇḍalī</s> remain after drawing in the opening of the liṅga?
Tell me, O eternal bliss, for you are omniscient, O lord of the gods.
Blessed <s>Śiva</s> said:
In the middle of the liṅga is a great radiance, fire-like, O beautiful one.

children.text: yat kiṃcid vāyuyogena brahmāṇḍo dahyate yataḥ
children.translated_text: Because, through some conjunction with breath, the brahmāṇḍa would be burned,

children.text: ataḥ sā kuṇḍalī devī mukhenācchādya saṃsthitā ||
children.translated_text: therefore that goddess <s>Kuṇḍalī</s> remains covering it with her mouth.
By that very means one should apply the bindu-śakti to the earthy liṅga.
Having raised the bindu-śakti, worship of the liṅga is proclaimed.
The blessed goddess said:
I have heard in the Nityātantra the great mantra of <s>Tripurā</s>.

children.text: idānīṃ śrotum icchāmi navārṇasya ca vāsanām ||
children.translated_text: Now I wish to hear the contemplation of the navārṇa mantra.
Blessed <s>Śiva</s> said:

children.text: bhūmiś candraḥ śivo māyā śaktiḥ kṛśānusādanau
children.translated_text: Earth, moon, <s>Śiva</s>, Māyā, Śakti, fire, and the two terminators,
the half-moon and the bindu: this is called the nine-syllabled meru.
By muttering the earth-seed alone, one quickly becomes a lord of the earth.
By muttering the moon-seed alone, one obtains great beauty.
By muttering the <s>Śiva</s>-seed alone, one moves on earth like <s>Śiva</s>.
When uttered together, truly, it bestows the fruits of the four aims of life.
The blessed goddess said:
O lord, what you have described as yoga-knowledge and the like is dissolution,

children.text: yāvat kāmādi saṃdīpyo bhāvayogo na labhyate ||
children.translated_text: so long as desire and the rest are inflamed and the yoga of bhāva is not obtained.
The great yogin whose seed flows upward, and below that through union with śakti,

children.text: brūhi me jagatāṃnātha kathaṃ dīrghāyuṣaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: tell me, O lord of the worlds, how he may become long-lived.
<s>Śrī Śiva</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi yena dīrghāyuṣaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Listen, O goddess; I shall explain that by which one becomes long-lived.

children.text: śrutvā gopaya yatnena na prakāśyaṃ kadācana ||
children.translated_text: Having heard it, guard it carefully. It is never to be revealed.

children.text: pūjayet kālikāṃ devīṃ tāriṇīṃ vātha sundarīm
children.translated_text: One should worship the goddess <s>Kālikā</s>, or <s>Tāriṇī</s>, or <s>Sundarī</s>,
with the sixteen services and with the five tattvas, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
Having worshiped for three days, one should then contemplate the six cakras.
After that, O <s>Parameśānī</s>, one should practice the garland-mantra.
Whether it is the <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> or the great preceding one, one should perform the practice on the petals.
On the four-petalled lotus one should recite eight times; on the six-petalled, twelve times.
On the ten-petalled, twenty times; on the twelve-petalled, the number of the Vedas and eyes.
On the sixteen-petalled, the number ten; four times, and on the two-petalled, eight.
With kumbhaka (breath-retention), O queen of the gods, one should recite the mantra in six garlands.
In this sequence, O mistress of the gods, when his life becomes firm,
he should recite on a rosary, by which he becomes a conqueror of death.
<s>Śrī Devī</s> said:
From the mūla-cakra up to the head is called the <s>Suṣumnā</s>.

children.text: tadgarbhasthā ca yā śaktiḥ sā devī kuṇḍarūpikā ||
children.translated_text: The śakti situated within it is the goddess in coiled form.
The goddess <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s> is always adorned with the fifty phonemes.

children.text: mālārūpā kathaṃ deva iti me saṃśayo hṛdi ||
children.translated_text: How, O god, is she in the form of a garland? This doubt is in my heart.
<s>Śrī Śiva</s> said:
In the thousand-spoked great lotus, in the seed-sheath, in the abode of <s>Śiva</s>,
one should bring her together by the haṃsa and the yoga of breath, with inhalation.

children.text: sahasrāraṃ tu samprāpya śivaṃ dṛṣṭvā tu kāminī
children.translated_text: Having reached the sahasrāra and having seen <s>Śiva</s>, the lovely one
always encircles that liṅga in the form of a garland, as <s>Kuṇḍalī</s>.
From the letter a up to la, and kṣa joined with the mouth,
the final syllable with an aperture, the lovely one with her own tail
pierces with her own tail the serpent-noose above it.
When <s>Kuṇḍalī</s> pervades this causal principle and remains established,
then indeed one should recite the mantra; he obtains immortality.
At exhalation, when the lovely goddess is entering her own abode,
one should not recite the mantra there; from recitation he would meet death.
During exhalation the garland is broken; this is true, O you honored by the gods.

children.text: chinne sūtre bhavenmṛtyuḥ puraiva kathitaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: When the thread is broken, death occurs; this was already told by me before.

children.text: iti te kathitaṃ kānte yato mṛtyuṃjayo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Thus it has been told to you, O beloved, how one becomes a conqueror of death.
Or else, carefully fixing one's gaze on the tip of one's own nose,
and carefully restraining the breath, one should utter it in a single pronunciation:
the garland-mantra, or the <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s>, or likewise the eighteen-syllabled mantra.
If one recites the mantra a thousand times every day, O <s>Pārvatī</s>,

children.text: jitvā mṛtyuṃ jarāṃ rogaṃ dīrghakālaṃ sa jīvati
children.translated_text: having conquered death, old age, and disease, he lives for a long time.
Apart from this, the great yoga is not obtained by one who seeks enjoyment.
Or else, O <s>Parameśānī</s>, according to the rule taught in the Ḍāmara,
one should carefully worship the goddess <s>Kātyāyanī</s>, preceded by the bhūtas.

children.text: tadā pañcasahasrābdaṃ niścitaṃ tu sa jīvati
children.translated_text: Then he certainly lives for five thousand years.
Thus I have told you everything that is the means of protecting the body.

children.text: na bhogī bhogamāpnoti yogī yogo na labhyate
children.translated_text: The enjoyer does not obtain enjoyment; the yogin does not obtain yoga.
By this truth, O mistress of the gods, enjoyment surely turns into yoga.
<s>Śrī Devī</s> said:

children.text: yanmālāyāṃ japenaiva kiṃ phalaṃ labhate naraḥ
children.translated_text: What fruit does a man obtain merely by recitation on that garland?
Tell me separately, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, the fruit of the garland of petals.
<s>Śrī Śiva</s> said:
One who desires the earth should recite the mantra in the fourfold mūlādhāra.
By recitation in the svādhiṣṭhāna, he soon becomes <s>Mahendra</s>.
By recitation in the maṇipūra, he becomes fit for heaven.
By recitation in the great lotus of the anāhata, he goes to the city of <s>Brahmā</s>.
By recitation in what is called the viśuddha, he certainly dwells in <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s world.

children.text: ājñācakre ca japtavye śvetadvīpe vaset sadā ||
children.translated_text: When recitation is performed in the ājñā-cakra, he always dwells in <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>.
That garland, O <s>Parameśānī</s>, is called the external garland.
The inner garland, the great garland, consists of the fifty phonemes.

children.text: māhātmyaṃ tasya deveśi kiṃ vaktuṃ śakyate mayā
children.translated_text: Its greatness, O mistress of the gods, how could I be able to describe?
If, having become steady in the sahasrāra, one recites eight hundred times,
a single part of a crore-fold portion of that fruit is known through another practice.
On earth his body becomes undecaying; there is no doubt at all.
One should recite the mantra on that garland for the sake of practice, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.

children.text: iti te kathitaṃ devi cirajīvī yathā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Thus I have told you, O goddess, how one may become long-lived.
Now, O <s>Parameśānī</s>, listen to <s>Bhūtakātyāyanī</s>.

children.text: vedādyaṃ śabdabījaṃ ca mahāmāyāṃ tataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: First comes the Vedic syllable, then the word-seed, and after that <s>Mahāmāyā</s>.
A pair of astras and the wife of fire: this supreme mantra is seven-syllabled.

children.text: śrīśivo'sya ṛṣiḥ prokto virāṭ chanda udāhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī Śiva</s> is declared to be its seer, and Virāṭ is stated as its meter.
The goddess <s>Bhūtakātyāyanī</s> always bestows dharma, wealth, and desire.

children.text: praṇavena ṣaḍaṅgaṃ ca prāṇāyāmaṃ ca sundari ||
children.translated_text: With the praṇava one should perform the six limbs and prāṇāyāma, O <s>Sundarī</s>.
I shall explain her meditation; listen respectfully, O <s>Sundarī</s>.
One should visualize her as fair-colored, with loose hair, adorned with all ornaments,
clothed in silk garments, her eyes always rolling,
holding in her left hand a skull-bowl filled with blood, and in her right hand
a golden vessel filled with liquor, adorned with a necklace around her neck,
shining like the autumn moon, radiant down to the toes of her feet.

children.text: evaṃ tāṃ varadāṃ nityāṃ bhāvayet siddhihetave
children.translated_text: Thus one should visualize her, the eternal giver of boons, for the sake of siddhi.
Then, O goddess, one should place the common arghya on one's own left side.
Having performed rites such as <s>jīvanyāsa</s> (installation of the life-principle), one should worship the supreme goddess,
O beautiful one, with the sixteenfold service and with the five tattvas.
With great effort one should worship her in the middle of the house for three days.
Then one should mutter the great mantra one thousand times, ending with the elephant-destroyer.
After that one should worship the goddess in an empty house for three days,
and each day one should mutter the mantra one thousand times, ending with the elephant-destroyer.

children.text: eva kṛte maheśāni yadi siddhirna jāyate
children.translated_text: When this has been done, O <s>Maheśānī</s>, if success does not arise,
then one should mutter the mantra in the ancestral ground for three days.

children.text: tataḥ siddhirbhaved devi satyaṃ satyaṃ hi supriye
children.translated_text: Then success will arise, O goddess. Truly, truly, O dearly beloved.
That statement, a statement of supplication, has been uttered by me in the work called <s>Ḍāmara</s>.
The blessed goddess said:
Tell me the great mudrā called <s>Kākīcañcu</s>, O treasure of compassion,
by the form of which, O lord of gods, one becomes intent on the body-seat.
Blessed <s>Śiva</s> said:
Without agitation, O queen of the gods, with the utmost effort

children.text: tālumūle nyaset paścāt tato vāyuṃ pibet śanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should first place the tongue at the root of the palate; then one should drink in the breath slowly.
Pressing the teeth against the teeth, one should practice <s>Kākīcañcu</s>.
By the procedure taught for the many-yoni posture, one should accomplish all rites.
Now then I shall explain the small yoni posture; listen, beloved.
One should place the right ankle at the anal opening and the liṅga at the joint.
Or one should hold the ankle at the navel aperture with the left hand.
By the procedure taught for the many-yoni posture, one should complete everything else.

children.text: mudrā caitanyatantre ca māhātmyaṃ kathitaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: In the <s>Caitanyatantra</s> I have described this mudrā and its greatness.
As is golden <s>Meru</s>, O goddess, and as is a swift-flowing river,

children.text: candrādikaṃ yathā devi cirajīvī tathā bhavet
children.translated_text: so, O goddess, beginning with the moon, one becomes long-lived.
The blessed goddess said:

children.text: daśāvatāraṃ deveśa brūhi me jagatāṃ guro ||
children.translated_text: O lord of gods, O teacher of the worlds, tell me the ten avatāras.
Now I wish to hear this; tell it in full detail.

children.text: kā vā devī kathaṃbhūtā vada me parameśvara ||
children.translated_text: Which goddess is she, and what is she like? Tell me, O supreme lord.
Blessed <s>Śiva</s> said:
The goddess <s>Tārā</s> is dark-blue in form; <s>Vagalā</s> has the form of the tortoise.
<s>Dhūmāvatī</s> is the boar, and <s>Chinnamastā</s> is the lion-man form.
<s>Bhuvaneśvarī</s> is the dwarf; <s>Mātaṃgī</s> has the form of <s>Rāma</s>.
<s>Tripurā</s> is the son of <s>Jamadagni</s>, while <s>Bhairavī</s> is <s>Balabhadra</s>.

children.text: mahālakṣmīr bhavet buddho durgā syāt kalkirūpiṇī
children.translated_text: <s>Mahālakṣmī</s> becomes the <s>Buddha</s>, and <s>Durgā</s> has the form of <s>Kalki</s>.
The blessed <s>Kālī</s> herself has arisen in the form of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text: iti te kathitaṃ devyavatāraṃ daśamameva hi
children.translated_text: Thus I have told you precisely the ten avatāras of the goddesses.
By worshiping these, O goddess, one becomes equal to <s>Mahādeva</s>.

children.text: āsāṃ dhyānādikaṃ sarvaṃ kathitaṃ me purā tava ||
children.translated_text: Their visualization and the rest of their practice have all been told by me to you before.
